color_rules.title: Warm Undertone Color Guide
color_rules.content: People with warm undertones look best in colors that reflect warmth: navy blue, olive green, cream, camel, burgundy, deep green, terracotta, mustard yellow, and earthy browns. These colors create harmony with the golden or yellow hues in warm skin. Avoid icy pastels, lavender, and stark white.

color_rules.title: Cool Undertone Color Guide
color_rules.content: Cool undertones are enhanced by colors with blue or pink bases: royal blue, charcoal grey, black, white, emerald green, cool purple, silver, and soft pink. These colors complement the pink or blue hues in cool skin. Avoid orange, earthy browns, and warm yellows.

color_rules.title: Neutral Undertone — Best Colors
color_rules.content: Neutral undertones have the most flexibility. Most colors work well — navy, forest green, burgundy, camel, slate grey, rose, cream, and white. Neutral undertones can experiment with both warm and cool palettes.

color_rules.title: Medium Skin Tone Best Colors
color_rules.content: Medium skin tones (olive, wheatish, tan) look stunning in jewel tones: navy blue, deep emerald, burgundy, forest green, and royal purple. Earth tones like olive, camel, and chocolate brown also work beautifully. Avoid very light pastels that may wash out the complexion.

color_rules.title: Dark Skin Tone Best Colors
color_rules.content: Darker skin tones are complemented by rich, vibrant colors: bright cobalt blue, deep red, emerald green, mustard yellow, burnt orange, and warm cream. These colors create beautiful contrast. White and cream also look striking. Avoid dark brown or very dark colors that reduce contrast.

color_rules.title: Light Skin Tone Best Colors
color_rules.content: Light skin tones are enhanced by deep, rich colors that provide contrast: navy, dark green, burgundy, maroon, charcoal, and black. Pastels can also work for casual occasions. Avoid very light or pale colors that blend with the skin.

color_rules.title: Eid Outfit Color Guide
color_rules.content: For Eid, choose celebratory and elegant colors. Traditional favorites include white, cream, navy, deep green, maroon, and royal blue. Shalwar Kameez or Kurta in these shades paired with embroidery is ideal. Avoid overly casual or Western-only looks for Eid morning prayer. For Eid gatherings, festive tones like gold, rich burgundy, and teal are excellent.

color_rules.title: Wedding — Baraat Colors
color_rules.content: For Baraat (wedding day), the groom traditionally wears Sherwani. Popular colors: cream, gold, maroon, navy, black, teal, and beige. Rich embroidery is important. The look should be regal and memorable. Sherwanis should ideally be paired with matching or contrasting churidar pajama and dupatta.

color_rules.title: Mehndi Night Colors
color_rules.content: Mehndi night calls for festive, vibrant colors. Yellow, mustard, peach, orange, pink, and lime green are traditional choices. For men, embroidered kurtas in mustard, yellow, peach, or rose are popular. Avoid dark, formal colors on Mehndi night — it is a celebration of color.

color_rules.title: Interview and Office Outfit Guide
color_rules.content: For interviews, choose professional and authoritative colors: navy blue, charcoal grey, white, and light grey. A well-fitting suit or formal kurta in these shades projects confidence. Avoid bright colors, patterns, or casual fabrics for interviews. For office, business casual is appropriate: smart kurta or dress shirt in navy, grey, or white.

color_rules.title: Pakistani Fashion Color Rules
color_rules.content: Pakistani fashion heavily features white and cream for prayer wear, navy and deep green for formal events, maroon and red for weddings. Summer lawn fabrics are popular in lighter colors. Winter sees heavier fabrics in jewel tones. Sherwani is the quintessential formal wear for weddings and special events.

color_rules.title: Indian Festival Color Traditions
color_rules.content: Indian festivals celebrate color: saffron for courage, white for peace, green for prosperity. Diwali calls for warm golden, orange, or deep jewel tones. Weddings feature bright colors — royal blue, emerald, or maroon kurtas for men. Nehru jackets in navy or black add sophistication to wedding attire.

color_rules.title: Middle Eastern Thobe Color Guide
color_rules.content: Thobes are traditionally white for daily and prayer wear, symbolizing purity. For special occasions, cream and beige thobes with fine embroidery are preferred. A Bisht — the formal cloak — is worn over the Thobe for grand occasions like Eid, graduation, and weddings. Bisht colors: black with gold, camel brown, or navy with silver.

color_rules.title: Navy Blue — The Universal Flattering Color
color_rules.content: Navy blue is arguably the most universally flattering color for all skin tones and undertones. It provides depth without being as stark as black, works for both formal and semi-formal occasions, and suits Pakistani, Indian, Middle Eastern, and Western fashion styles. Navy kurtas, sherwanis, suits, and dress shirts all project elegance and authority.

color_rules.title: Color Combinations that Always Work
color_rules.content: Classic combinations: Navy + Cream (elegant), Olive + Cream (earthy), Maroon + Gold (regal), Black + White (timeless), Deep Green + Cream (fresh formal), Charcoal + Light Blue (smart casual), Burgundy + Beige (warm sophisticated). These pairings create balanced, visually appealing outfits for any occasion.
